title: Direct Variation
student_objective: I can write and solve equations that model direct variation.

concept_cards.title: Direct variation form
concept_cards.content: Direct variation has the form y=kx. The constant k is the constant of variation and also the slope.

concept_cards.title: Passes through the origin
concept_cards.content: Because y=kx has no added constant, x=0 gives y=0. Every direct variation graph passes through (0,0).

concept_cards.title: Find k
concept_cards.content: For any nonzero input, k=y/x. A constant y/x ratio across points signals direct variation.

concept_cards.title: Use the model
concept_cards.content: Once k is known, substitute the requested x-value into y=kx to find the corresponding output.

identify_direct.teacher_signal: Student confuses y=kx with y=mx+b where b is nonzero.

constant_k.teacher_signal: Student uses x/y instead of y/x or changes the ratio.

application.teacher_signal: Student does not connect the constant of variation to a real rate.

items.prompt: Does y=4x represent direct variation? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Look for y=kx with no added constant.
hint_steps: Direct variation must look like y=kx.
Yes, it is direct variation with k=4.

solution_steps.explanation: So the relation is direct variation.

items.prompt: For y=7x, what is the constant of variation k?
items.tutor_behavior: k is the coefficient of x in y=kx.

items.prompt: y varies directly with x. If y=18 when x=6, write the direct variation equation.
The points (2,10), (4,20), and (6,30) lie on a relation. Does it show direct variation?
A worker earns $72 for 6 hours at a constant hourly rate. Model earnings E as a direct variation of hours h.
items.tutor_behavior: Hourly earnings are proportional to hours worked.

items.prompt: y varies directly with x. If y=28 when x=7, write the equation.
items.tutor_behavior: Divide y by x to find k.

items.prompt: Does y=6x+2 represent direct variation? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Direct variation must pass through the origin.
hint_steps: Direct variation has no added constant.
No; y=6x+2 is not direct variation.

solution_steps.explanation: The graph does not pass through the origin.

items.prompt: A recipe uses 9 cups of water for 3 cups of rice. If water W varies directly with rice r, write the model.
items.tutor_behavior: Use water per cup of rice as k.
hint_steps: k=3 cups water per cup rice.

items.prompt: y varies directly with x. If y=-15 when x=5, write the equation.
items.tutor_behavior: A negative output for positive x can give a negative k.

items.prompt: The points (1,4), (2,8), and (3,13) are given. Is this direct variation?
items.tutor_behavior: Check all y/x ratios, not just the first two.
hint_steps: No; the ratio y/x is not constant.

solution_steps.explanation: The ratios are not all equal.
A direct variation needs one constant k.

items.prompt: A car travels 210 miles in 3.5 hours at constant speed. Model distance d as a direct variation of time t.
items.tutor_behavior: Constant speed is a direct-variation rate.

solution_steps.explanation: Write distance as rate times time.

items.prompt: y varies directly with x. If y=45 when x=9, write the equation.
A machine fills 84 bottles in 7 minutes at a constant rate. Model bottles B as a direct variation of minutes m.
A direct variation contains the point (-4,18). Write its equation.
items.tutor_behavior: Use k=y/x even when x is negative.

items.prompt: Does the relation through (0,3) and (2,9) represent direct variation?
items.tutor_behavior: A direct variation must include the origin.

solution_steps.explanation: It does not pass through the origin.
